prompt:
Desktop web application UI comp at 1536 by 1024, not a poster and not a photograph. Product: Infrastructure AI Agent, an operations workspace for multiple bridge inspection runs. Direction: Corridor Command Map, drawing from transport control maps, work-zone boards, route diagrams, and precise engineering interfaces. Restrained palette only: mist gray #E8ECE8 page, near-black green #18231F text, route teal #176B62, work-zone amber #E1B13D, white working surfaces. No gradients, no glass, no decorative imagery, no sample images, no huge headline, no floating card grid.

Composition A: a 280px full-height left rail containing compact brand, a prominent New inspection action, search/filter controls, and a dense vertical list of six inspection runs with asset name, run ID fragment, stage, percent, and status dot. One running item is selected. The remaining wide workspace begins with a slim case header showing bridge name, location, severity, repair required, and export action. Directly below is a horizontal workflow route labeled Intake, Evidence, Severity, RAG, Planning, Scheduling, Report, with completed nodes solid teal, current node amber, future nodes outlined. Under the route is a tab bar: Overview, Observations, RAG Sources, Maintenance Plan, Schedule, Report, Activity. The Overview tab is active and uses an asymmetric engineering layout: large observation summary and evidence trace on the left, narrower decision summary and live progress on the right. Bottom area hints at retrieved sources and maintenance tasks. Use thin route lines, square-ish 4-6px corners, compact sans typography, tabular numbers, visible focus and status labels. High information density but calm and clean. All text is plausible real UI copy; no marketing language.

The interface should look production-ready, precise, and distinctly made for bridge inspection operations. Show clear hierarchy, whitespace, and realistic control sizes.
